questions.q: The man exclaimed that his wallet was stolen.
o: "My wallet was stolen!" the man said.
"Somebody stole my wallet!" exclaimed the man.
The man exclaimed, "My wallet was stolen!"
The man cried, "My wallet was stolen."
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — The man exclaimed, “My wallet was stolen!”
The task is to change the indirect statement into direct speech. The possessive “his” changes to “my” because the speaker is referring to his own wallet. The exclamatory reporting verb is retained in option C, which is the option marked by the MPSC final key.
Source check: Series I, Question 26; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: Mr. Swer asked the lady if she could tell him where the nearest post office is.
o: "Where is the nearest post office?" Mr. Swer asked the lady.
Mr. Swer asked the lady, "Could you tell me where the nearest post office is?"
Mr. Swer asked the lady, "Where is the nearest post office?"
Mr. Swer said to the lady, "Where is the nearest post office?"
questions.e:
Correct answer: B — Mr. Swer asked the lady, “Could you tell me where the nearest post office is?”
This direct-speech option expresses the same polite request. The embedded clause “where the nearest post office is” keeps statement word order after the question phrase. The MPSC final key marks option B.
Source check: Series I, Question 29; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: The Professor said that nobody could solve the problem.
o: The Professor said, "Nobody can solve the problem."
The Professor said, "Nobody could solve the problem."
The Professor exclaimed, "Nobody could solve the problem."
The Professor exclaimed, "Nobody can solve the problem."
questions.e:
Official final-key answer: D — The Professor exclaimed, “Nobody can solve the problem.”
The printed question asks for the direct form of the indirect statement. The MPSC final answer key marks D. Editorial caution: “exclaimed” is an unusual reporting verb for this plain declarative statement, but the official keyed option is retained exactly rather than silently replaced with a more natural construction.
Source check: Series I, Question 30; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: The speaker's ___ remarks left the audience in awe; his words were both profound and enlightening.
questions.e:
Correct answer: B — pithy.
“Pithy” means brief but full of meaning or force. The sentence describes remarks that were profound and enlightening, so “pithy” fits. “Mundane” and “banal” mean ordinary or unoriginal; “insipid” means lacking interest or flavour.
Source check: Series I, Question 51; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: The novel's plot was so ___ that readers were hooked from the first page, unable to predict the twists in the plot.
questions.e:
Correct answer: B — engrossing.
“Engrossing” means absorbing or highly interesting. A plot that hooks readers from the first page is engrossing. “Formulaic” suggests predictable, which conflicts with the sentence's reference to unexpected twists.
Source check: Series I, Question 52; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: While her sister was ___ and thrifty, Maria was notoriously extravagant, spending money without a second thought.
questions.e:
Correct answer: A — frugal.
“Frugal” means careful and economical in spending. It matches “thrifty” and contrasts with Maria's extravagant spending. “Lavish” and “prodigal” suggest excessive spending.
Source check: Series I, Question 53; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: The government will ___ the new policy next week, aiming to improve transparency across departments.
questions.e:
Correct answer: A — adopt.
“To adopt a policy” means to formally accept or put it into effect. “Adapt” means modify something to suit a purpose; “adept” is an adjective meaning skilled; “admit” means acknowledge or allow entry.
Source check: Series I, Question 54; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: The officer's ___ response to the confrontational question demonstrated her skill in handling complex and sensitive situations.
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — tempered.
“Tempered” can describe a response that is moderated, controlled or restrained. The sentence praises the officer's ability to handle a difficult question calmly. “Temperamental” means prone to unpredictable changes of mood.
Source check: Series I, Question 55; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: Her remarks were intended to be pacifying, but they were interpreted as ___ by the opposition.
questions.e:
Correct answer: A — provocative.
“Pacifying” means calming or reducing anger. “Provocative” means likely to cause annoyance, anger or a strong reaction, so it expresses the contrast in the sentence.
Source check: Series I, Question 56; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: Unlike the ___ forest they had left behind, the desert landscape was desiccated and bereft of life.
questions.e:
Correct answer: B — verdant.
“Verdant” means green with vegetation. It contrasts with a desert landscape described as desiccated and bereft of life. “Arid” and “desolate” are closer to the description of the desert.
Source check: Series I, Question 57; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: She ___ her mother's stubbornness, always refusing to back down once she's made up her mind.
questions.e:
Correct answer: A — takes after.
“To take after” someone means to resemble that person, often in appearance or character. The sentence says she shares her mother's stubbornness. The other phrasal verbs do not express resemblance.
Source check: Series I, Question 58; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: The research team had to ___ their procedure after the Superintendent pointed out several errors in their experimental design.
questions.e:
Correct answer: A — revise.
“To revise” means to review and make changes or corrections. Since errors were identified in the experimental design, the team had to revise the procedure. Repeating it without changes would not address the errors.
Source check: Series I, Question 59; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: The negotiations reached a complete ___, with neither side willing to compromise on their fundamental demands.
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — impasse.
An “impasse” is a deadlock or situation in which no progress is possible. The sentence says neither side is willing to compromise, so negotiations have reached an impasse. “Accord” means agreement.

questions.q: The prisoner was released on ___ for good behaviour.
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — parole.
“Parole” is the conditional release of a prisoner, usually subject to supervision and conditions, before the full sentence has been served. “Bail” generally concerns release while a case is pending.
Source check: Series I, Question 61; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: Life is to death as pleasure is to ___.
questions.e:
Correct answer: A — suffering.
The analogy pairs a concept with its opposite: life is contrasted with death, so pleasure is contrasted with suffering. Bliss and ecstasy are closer in meaning to pleasure.
Source check: Series I, Question 62; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: Please do not ___ an offer made by the Chairman.
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — refuse.
“To refuse an offer” means to decline it. “Refute” means to prove a statement or argument wrong; “refrain” is normally followed by “from” and means hold back from doing something.
Source check: Series I, Question 63; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: The police ___ the mob.
questions.e:
Correct answer: D — dispersed.
“To disperse” means to scatter or cause a crowd to move apart. In this sentence, “The police dispersed the mob” is the intended construction. The other options do not convey scattering the crowd.

questions.q: Robert was ___ with a natural talent for music.
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — endowed.
“Endowed with” means naturally provided with a quality, ability or gift. The standard expression is “endowed with a natural talent.”

questions.q: If you drink too much, it will ___ your judgement.
questions.e:
Correct answer: B — impair.
“To impair” means to weaken or damage the quality or effectiveness of something. Excessive drinking can impair judgement. “Impede” means obstruct progress; “impose” means place a burden or requirement; “impel” means drive or urge.
Source check: Series I, Question 66; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.

questions.q: It is very ___ to miss one's train by half a minute.
questions.e:
Correct answer: D — exasperating.
“Exasperating” means extremely irritating or frustrating. Missing a train by only half a minute is particularly frustrating. “Annoying” is a possible general description, but the official key selects the stronger word “exasperating.”
Source check: Series I, Question 67; official final answer key dated 17-12-2025.
